newsitem.title: JAPAN: Palladium seen supported by large short positions.
newsitem.headline: Palladium seen supported by large short positions.

text.p: Large short positions held by private investors in Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) futures are likely to support palladium prices, although the price outlook depends on the resumption of Russian metal exports, Japanese traders said on Thursday.
"When the timing of the Japan-Russia platinum group metal export contract talks is established, palladium may come under selling pressure temporarily," a trading house trader said.
"But support may be solid as private investors may have to cover massive shorts after all," a trader at a trading house said.

Japan-Russia export contract talks for platinum group metals for 1997 were supposed to have been held in the middle of December 1996, but have been indefinitely postponed due to Russian budget problems and government changes.
Japanese traders have yet to hear from Russia's export agency as to when the talks may be held.
Traders said private investors' short positions totalled more than 25,000 lots for all TOCOM palladium futures, out of total open interest of 100,885 lots as of April 2.
Private investors have built up short positions since the benchmark TOCOM palladium was at about the 460 yen per gram earlier this year, they said.
Supported by uncertainty over Russian metal supplies, the TOCOM benchmark palladium contract hit an all-time high of 597 yen per gram on March 12. It had retreated to 564 yen by Tuesday.
Dollar-based palladium prices, which rose above $160 per ounce in mid-March for the first time in 1-1/2 years, retreated to $145.75/146.64 in late Tokyo trade on Thursday.

"The physical palladium market is basically tight on the disruption of Russia's metal exports. I think palladium prices will not fall at least until Russian shipments arrive in Japan," another trading house trader said. He put near-term support at $140 per ounce.
The trader said that even if the timing of the talks is decided, availability of Russian metal supplies to meet exports is a concern.--Tokyo Commodity Desk, +81-3-3432-7431
